newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 18.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Friday:
* Another overnight rate cut on Thursday and a stronger currency will prompt short-term rallies, traders said.
* "At least two more days of upticks, accompanied by substantial volume will give a clearer picture of market prospects," said Sun Hung Kai Securities in its daily outlook.
* BPI Securities Corp said buying of selected fundamentally sound issues would provide long-term opportunities.
* On Thursday, the Philippine composite index snapped out of a two-day losing streak ending 33.02 points at 2,620.38.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 18.11 points lower at 8,020.77. PLDT's ADR closed down $0 7/8 at $32 3/4.
* The Philippine peso ended at 28 pesos to a dollar vs 29.30.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average at 28.1875 percent vs 32.1875 percent.

* The Central Bank said on Thursday it was cutting its overnight borrowing rate to 25 percent from 28 percent effective July 18. It will also lower its overnight lending rate to 27 percent from 30 percent.
* The Bankers Association of the Philippines said all commercial banks had agreed to further cut their over-the-counter (OTC) dollar selling rates.
* Philippine inflation is projected to remain at an average of six to seven percent this year, as the peso slowly recovers to 28.00 to the dollar on Thursday, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson.
* The Philippines will use the International Monetary Fund's $1.05 billion financial package, CB governor Singson said.
* The Central Bank was selling dollars at 29 pesos in early trading.
* The Philippine trade deficit was at $4.727 bilion in the first five months of the year from $5.09 billion in the same period last year.
* The Bureau of Treasury said it had decided to offer more short-term bills next week because of the prevailing high interest rates.

* Two of the largest banks in the country, Far East Bank and Trust Co and Bank of the Phlippine Islands said they had lowered their prime lending rates following the cut in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 28 percent.
